title: 6 Best Residency Management Software Tools for GME Programs
description: Scheduling Wizard and 5 other residency management software tools for GME programs, compare New Innovations, QGenda, MedHub.
content:
If you've ever heard a chief resident say "my brain is so tired of all this thinking!", you're not alone. Running a residency program comes with a lot of logistics. Between building call schedules that don't violate ACGME duty hour rules, coordinating clinic blocks, tracking resident evaluations, and staying ready for an accreditation site visit, the administrative load is relentless.

The promise of residency management software is simple: automate the chaos. In practice, many GME programs use two or three tools, one for scheduling, one for evaluations, one for compliance reporting, because each category is built for a different job.

This guide reviews six tools for GME programs, covering scheduling, evaluations, credentialing, and ACGME compliance. Whether you're a program director evaluating enterprise platforms or a chief resident who just wants to stop spending 40 hours a year building a schedule in Excel, there's a right answer for your situation, and it probably isn't the same answer for everyone.

A note before the list: we are Scheduling Wizard. We build physician schedules as a service, so we have included ourselves below and you should read our entry with that in mind. The order here is by one thing only, who actually builds the schedule, which is why a service comes first and the software and the platforms you publish through follow. Rank by cost, or by how good the mobile app is, and the order changes. We have described the other tools as their own users and documentation describe them.

What GME Administrators Actually Need from Residency Management Software

Before comparing tools, it helps to define the core functional categories that matter in Graduate Medical Education:

  • Scheduling: Building and distributing block rotations, call schedules, clinic assignments, and attending coverage, while respecting ACGME duty hour limits, program-specific rules, and resident preferences.
  • Evaluations: Automating the feedback loop between residents, faculty, and program directors, and tracking progress against ACGME Milestones.
  • Credentialing: Verifying trainee licenses, certifications, and onboarding documentation.
  • ACGME Compliance: Documenting work hours, tracking the Common Program Requirements, and generating the reports needed for accreditation.

These categories are built differently. An evaluation platform built for milestone tracking is a different thing from a team that builds fair call schedules. It helps to know which job you are buying for.

The 6 Residency Management Software Tools

1. Scheduling Wizard: Best for Done-for-You Schedule Creation

Type: Managed Scheduling Service
Best for: Programs that want the schedule build taken off their plate entirely.

Scheduling Wizard is the one on this list that isn't software in the traditional sense. It's a YC-backed managed service, meaning a team builds the schedule for you rather than handing you a platform to operate.

Your program sends its rules (staffing requirements, resident preferences, ACGME duty hour rules, subspecialty-specific restrictions) and Scheduling Wizard delivers complete Block, Clinic, Call, and Attending schedules as Excel or Google Sheets, or on a custom live view we build for you. There is no login to learn or rule setup to maintain, and nothing to retrain when your chief resident graduates.

Key features:

  • The ACGME requirements built in while the schedule is made, not flagged afterwards
  • Full schedule types covered, Block/Rotation, Call, Clinic, and Attending schedules
  • Delivered as Excel or Google Sheets, or on a custom live view; upload it into the platform you already use, use the live view, or both
  • Continuity: your program's rules and preferences are kept year over year, so they do not leave with each chief
  • Fair call distribution: equitable distribution of night shifts, call burden, and post-clinic assignments part of the build
  • Redrafts around unplanned absences and last-minute changes

Scheduling Wizard is first here because it addresses the problem most programs actually struggle with: not viewing a schedule, but creating one that is fair, within the rules, and complete. Programs that hand us the build spend their time reviewing drafts rather than building them.

Website: schedulingwiz.com

What you get: finished block, call, clinic and attending schedules in the format your program wants, as Excel or Google Sheets, with a custom live view if you want one. Major redrafts through the year are included. For the specifics, see our page on residency management software. We build to your rules and requests, however granular, with the ACGME requirements among them.

2. MedHub: Best All-in-One RMS for Evaluations & Accreditation

Type: All-in-One Residency Management Software
Best for: Institutions that need a centralized platform for evaluations, milestone tracking, work hours reporting, and accreditation readiness.

MedHub is an enterprise GME platform focused on program quality and accreditation. If your main need is managing evaluations and staying ready for review, it is a natural one to look at.

Key features:

  • Automated evaluation workflows with ACGME milestone tracking and multi-source feedback (peer, patient, faculty)
  • Work hours logging with detailed compliance reporting
  • Centralized accreditation data for program reviews and site visits
  • API integration with scheduling platforms including QGenda
  • A mobile app for evaluations and work hour logging

Caveat: MedHub includes a scheduling module, but its focus is evaluations and accreditation. Programs with intricate call or block scheduling needs often use it alongside a dedicated scheduling solution.

3. QGenda: Best for Enterprise-Scale Schedule Management

Type: Self-Service Scheduling Software
Best for: Large academic medical centers and health systems that need enterprise-grade scheduling integrated with HR, payroll, and credentialing systems.

QGenda is a cloud-based workforce management platform used in large health systems. It centralizes scheduling across departments, automates notifications, and connects scheduling data to downstream systems like payroll and credentialing.

Key features:

  • Cloud-based schedule creation and viewing
  • Automated notifications and real-time schedule access
  • Enterprise integrations with HR, payroll, and credentialing platforms
  • Analytics and reporting on staffing and provider availability

Caveat: QGenda is a powerful self-service tool, meaning someone at your program needs to learn it, configure it, and operate it. That operational burden typically falls on the chief resident or a dedicated coordinator. Some programs keep QGenda for publishing and day-to-day management and hand the build to a service like Scheduling Wizard; the two work together.

4. New Innovations: Best User-Friendly All-in-One RMS

Type: All-in-One Residency Management Software
Best for: Programs looking for a balanced, relatively intuitive platform that covers scheduling, evaluations, work hours, and compliance in one place.

New Innovations is a long-established residency management platform that covers scheduling, evaluations, work hours and compliance in one place.

Key features:

  • Integrated modules for scheduling, evaluations, procedure logging, and work hours
  • Customizable reporting for resident performance and program metrics
  • An interface many residents and faculty already know
  • Competency-based evaluation tools aligned to ACGME requirements

Caveat: Programs with complicated call structures or multi-department dependencies often still build the schedule outside it and bring it in.

5. Amion: Best Lightweight Publishing Platform

Type: Publishing Platform
Best for: Programs that need a simple, familiar way to publish and view on-call and daily schedules.

Amion is a familiar name in residency programs. Amion is built to publish and share the schedule rather than to build it. You build the schedule externally (in Excel, or via a service like Scheduling Wizard), then put it into Amion so your team can see it from any device.

Key features:

  • Simple, familiar web and mobile interface for viewing call and daily schedules
  • Real-time updates once a schedule is uploaded
  • Familiar to many residents

Caveat: Amion is where the schedule is published and looked up; building it still happens somewhere else.

6. Lightning Bolt by PerfectServe: Best for Complex Shift-Based Call Scheduling

Type: Self-Service Scheduling Software
Best for: Departments with complex, shift-based call patterns that want automated schedule generation with the ability to make manual edits.

Lightning Bolt generates schedules from rules the department defines, and is often used by call-heavy departments with complex shift patterns.

Key features:

  • Rules-based scheduling engine that generates schedules from user-defined rules
  • Flexible call scheduling with support for complex coverage patterns
  • Manual override capability for direct schedule adjustments
  • Integration with PerfectServe's broader communication platform

Caveat: This is still a self-service tool. The operational burden doesn't disappear; it shifts to whoever manages the software. Someone at the program still has to write the rules, keep them current and review the output.

The Distinction That Actually Matters: Schedule Creation vs. Schedule Management

Most GME software conversations conflate two different problems: creating a schedule and managing one. Understanding the gap between these two is the clearest lens for making the right purchasing decision.

Self-service scheduling tools (QGenda, Lightning Bolt, New Innovations) give you infrastructure. You still have to drive it. That means a chief resident or coordinator must:

  • Learn the platform
  • Correctly configure every rule
  • Run the build and review the output for errors
  • Manually verify ACGME compliance
  • Hand all of it over when the next chief resident takes over

With a managed scheduling service (Scheduling Wizard), someone else does the build. You describe what you need, and a finished schedule, built to your rules, arrives in your inbox. The expertise stays with the service provider, not trapped in one chief resident's brain.

For GME programs where scheduling eats a large part of the chief's year, where a chief resident is losing weeks of their year to Excel formulas and fairness disputes, the question is whether you want better tools for your scheduler or someone else doing the build.

Decision Framework: Choosing the Right Residency Management Software for Your Program

Start by identifying your biggest operational bottleneck.

Choose an all-in-one RMS (MedHub, New Innovations) if:

  • Your primary gaps are in evaluations, milestone tracking, or accreditation reporting
  • You need a centralized system of record for resident performance data
  • Your scheduling needs are relatively straightforward

Choose a self-service scheduling platform (QGenda, Lightning Bolt) if:

  • You have a dedicated, long-term scheduler (not a rotating chief) with bandwidth to become a platform expert
  • Your priority is hands-on control over the scheduling process
  • You need deep enterprise integrations with HR, payroll, or credentialing systems

Choose a specialized publishing platform (Amion) if:

  • You already have a schedule creation process in place and just need a simple, familiar way to distribute and publish it

Choose a managed service (Scheduling Wizard) if:

  • Your biggest pain is the time, complexity, and compliance risk of schedule creation itself
  • You need ACGME rules built in from the start, not just manual verification
  • You want to free your chief residents from administrative overload so they can focus on medicine
  • Your program loses critical scheduling knowledge every year with chief resident turnover

Which Kind of Tool Fits Your Program

If your biggest pain is schedule viewing or communication, there are solid tools for that. If your biggest pain is schedule creation and ACGME compliance, the actual process of building a fair schedule within the rules from scratch, then you're in a different category entirely.

Residency management software gives your team tools to do the work. Scheduling Wizard gives you the finished schedule, built by a team that has written down the ACGME requirements you tell us apply, your program's rules and your residents' requests. For programs that are done treating scheduling as a software problem and ready to treat it as a job someone else does, it is a different way of working.
